summary: John Peile worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Repton School, St Bees School, Christ's College, Cambridge (~1856–1860), and under Theodor Benfey (~1869–1870). His career included posts at Christ's College (~1860–1910), Cambridge (1884–1891), and Newnham College (~1890–1909).
John Pickford was an Indologist who studied under Monier Monier-Williams. He served as a professor at the University of Madras.

Powers specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, having studied at College of the Holy Cross, McMaster University, and University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, among others. He held posts at ANU, USF, Deakin University (2016–2022), and University of Melbourne (2022).

Campbell works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb, and studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Denma Lochö Rinpoche, and Gyumed Khensur Lobsang Ngawang.

John R. McRae worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Yale (~1975–1983) under Stanley Weinstein and studied under Seizan Yanagida. He taught at Cornell, Indiana University Bloomington (~1996–2005), and Komazawa University (~2005–2008).

John Ronald Newman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and later served as Assistant Professor of Asian Religions at New College of Florida.

John Ross Carter specialized in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at King's College London, SOAS, and Harvard University under Wilfred Cantwell Smith (~1965–1972), later spending his career as a professor at Colgate University (~1972–2006).

Strong is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Oberlin, Hartford Seminary, and the University of Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds. He was a professor at Bates College and held visiting professorships at Chicago, Harvard, Princeton, and Stanford.

John Shakespear worked in linguistics and Indology after studying under John Richardson. He held professorships at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst (1805–1809), and Addiscombe Military Seminary (1809–1829).
John Shore, 1st Baron Teignmouth, was active in Indology and history and archaeology. He succeeded William Jones and served as president of the Asiatic Society.

Hawley works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Amherst College (~1959–1963) and under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1970–1974). He held a post at Bowdoin College (~1974–1976) and became a professor at Columbia University around 1986.
John Stuart Mill worked in philosophy. He studied at University College London (~1828–1830) and held a post at the East India Company from around 1823 to 1858.

John Sydenham Furnivall worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Trinity Hall, Trinity College, and the University of Cambridge (~1896–1899), as well as Leiden University (~1923–1925), and held a post at Cambridge from around 1936 to 1941.

John Taber is an Indologist and philosopher. He earned his D. Phil. at the University of Hamburg (1973–1979) under Lambert Schmithausen and Reiner Wiehl, later holding positions at Case Western Reserve University (~1984–1989) and the University of New Mexico (~1989).

Platts was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies educated at Bedford School and Balliol College. He held teaching and administrative posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Saugor High School before becoming Teacher of Persian at Oxford (1880).

John Vincent Bellezza specializes in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied under tutor Yungdrung Tenzin and teacher Tshering Choephel, and was affiliated with the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences in 2014.

John W. Pettit works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Haverford College, completed doctoral work under Robert A. F. Thurman, and studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Lal Mani Joshi, Gunapala Dharmasiri, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

Schroeder works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Los Angeles Valley College and the University of Oregon under Don Levi, he held posts at Oregon (1993–1994), The College of Wooster (1994–1995), and St. Mary's College of Maryland (1996).

John W. Spellman worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Washington from around 1964 to 1967 and as a professor at the University of Windsor from around 1967 to 1999.

John Wilson worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies, and was educated at the University of Edinburgh (1819–1828). He served as president of the Literary Society of Bombay (~1835–1842) and vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1869).
